title: ITIN for US Gambling Winnings: 1042-S, 1040-NR and UK Refund Claims
description: A UK-focused guide to ITIN applications after US casino withholding, Form 1042-S, treaty review and the 1040-NR refund route.
body:
Did a US casino keep tax from your winnings even though you live and pay tax in the UK?

Martin returned from Las Vegas with a Form 1042-S showing federal tax withheld. The casino cannot tell him whether the UK-US treaty helps or how he can file without a US tax number.

Start with the evidence, not the refund promise

The gambling type, tax residence, payer documents and treaty position all matter. A refund is not automatic. Keep Form 1042-S, the casino statement, payment records, passport travel evidence and any W-2G issued.

Two possible ITIN routes

Exception 2(d) is a narrow at-source route using an appropriate gaming official acting as an IRS Acceptance Agent. If that route was not used, the IRS guide states that a nonresident can apply later with Form W-7 attached to Form 1040-NR and a copy of Form 1042-S showing the tax withheld.

What the return must establish

The 1040-NR should report the relevant winnings and withholding and identify any treaty article being claimed. The facts must support the position; an ITIN by itself does not create a refund.

Practical takeaway

  • Keep the 1042-S and casino evidence before leaving the United States.
  • Without an at-source gaming official, expect the W-7 and 1040-NR route.
  • Check treaty eligibility before relying on a refund estimate.

A reader asks

“The casino withheld 30%. Will I get all of it back?”

Not necessarily. Send us the 1042-S, gambling type, dates and UK residence details so the filing and treaty position can be reviewed.

Check my gambling withholding route →

title: ITIN for a US Inheritance or Estate Distribution Received in the UK
description: When a UK beneficiary may need an ITIN for a US estate distribution, withholding report, Form 1042-S or nonresident tax return.
body:
A US executor says they cannot release your inheritance without a US tax number. Does every overseas beneficiary really need an ITIN?

Amira lives in Birmingham and is due a distribution from her aunt's US estate. The fiduciary has asked for tax forms and may issue Form 1042-S.

An inheritance does not automatically create ITIN eligibility

The application needs a US federal tax purpose. That may arise where a fiduciary or withholding agent must report or withhold on a current-year distribution, or where the beneficiary must file Form 1040-NR.

Possible Exception 1(d) evidence

For a current-year distribution subject to federal withholding or IRS reporting, the IRS guide calls for an original document or signed letter from the withholding agent on official letterhead. It should identify the beneficiary and show that an ITIN is required for the distribution. A self-generated statement is not enough by itself.

Documents to collect

  • The executor, fiduciary or withholding-agent letter.
  • Any Form 1042-S or distribution statement.
  • Estate correspondence showing the beneficiary and expected payment.
  • Passport and any required return or exception evidence.

Practical takeaway

  • Ask the fiduciary why the ITIN is needed and what form will be filed.
  • Match the W-7 route to current-year reporting or a return.
  • Do not assume that being named in a will is enough.

A reader asks

“The executor only sent an email. Is that enough?”

Usually the exception evidence should be an original signed letter on official letterhead. Send us the correspondence and we will give the fiduciary a focused document checklist.

Review my inheritance documents →

title: ITIN for Amazon KDP Authors in the UK: Royalties, W-8BEN and Form W-7
description: When a UK self-published author may need an ITIN for US royalty reporting, what supports Exception 1(d), and why treaty rates are not automatic.
body:
Are US royalties being withheld from your book sales because your tax interview asks for a number you do not have?

Sophie publishes from Bristol and receives US-source royalties. Her publisher's tax dashboard asks for a US taxpayer identification number and a W-8BEN.

First confirm that an ITIN is actually required

A platform request does not by itself establish W-7 eligibility. Confirm the income type, the payer's current-year IRS reporting or withholding requirement, and whether the payer will provide suitable evidence.

Exception 1(d) for royalty distributions

The IRS guide permits an original document or signed withholding-agent letter on official letterhead showing the author's name and that an ITIN is required for current-year royalty payments subject to US reporting or withholding. A self-generated statement is accepted only with stronger supporting evidence such as the contract or a payer-sent document.

ITIN and W-8BEN do different jobs

The ITIN identifies the taxpayer. Form W-8BEN documents foreign status and any treaty claim to the payer. A treaty rate depends on the exact income and article; the ITIN alone does not guarantee a zero rate or refund.

Practical takeaway

  • Request a payer letter or official royalty evidence before filing W-7.
  • Use the correct current-year exception evidence.
  • Treat the W-8BEN and treaty analysis as separate from ITIN issuance.

A reader asks

“Can a screenshot of my royalty dashboard support the application?”

It may help explain the facts, but it may not satisfy the exception by itself. Send the contract, payer correspondence and statement so we can identify the strongest evidence.

Check my KDP royalty route →

title: What Is an ITIN? A Plain-English Guide for UK Residents
description: What is an ITIN number, who issues it, what it looks like and what it can and cannot do. A plain-English guide from UK-based IRS acceptance agents.
body:
A U.S. bank, a buyer or an IRS form has just asked you for your “ITIN”. You live in the UK and have never heard the word. Where do you even start?

Priya inherited a share of a U.S. rental property. The management company emailed: “We need your ITIN before the next payment.” She has no Social Security Number and no idea what an ITIN is.

What an ITIN actually is

An Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) is a tax processing number issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to certain resident and non-resident aliens, their spouses and their dependants. It is a nine-digit number that starts with 9 and is formatted like a Social Security Number (9XX-7X-XXXX). The fourth and fifth digits fall in set ranges (50–65, 70–88, 90–92 and 94–99).

Why the IRS issues them

Both resident and non-resident foreigners can have U.S. tax filing and payment duties. The IRS issues ITINs so people who cannot get a Social Security Number (SSN) can still file returns, pay tax and have payments properly accounted for.

What an ITIN does not do

  • It does not authorise you to work in the U.S.
  • It does not give you Social Security benefits or the Earned Income Tax Credit.
  • It does not change your immigration status.
  • It is not valid identification outside the tax system – never offer it as ID for non-tax purposes.

Do I need one?

If you are eligible for an SSN you must not apply for an ITIN. If you cannot get an SSN but must give the IRS (or a U.S. payer) a taxpayer ID, you apply on Form W-7. The ITIN then goes in the space for the SSN on your U.S. return.

Practical takeaway

  • An ITIN is a 9-digit U.S. tax number for people who cannot get an SSN.
  • It is for tax purposes only: no work rights, no immigration effect.
  • Use Form W-7; apply with a U.S. tax return unless a listed exception applies.

A reader asks

“I live in Manchester and a U.S. company wants my ITIN. Can I apply from the UK without travelling to the States?”

Yes. You can apply by post, or through an IRS acceptance agent in the UK who can check your documents in person and send the package to the IRS.

title: Why Do I Need an ITIN? 10 Common Reasons for UK-Based Applicants
description: Spouse of a U.S. citizen, LLC, partnership, U.S. bank account, 401(k), property sale, treaty benefits, renewal and more: the real reasons people need an ITIN.
body:
Is an ITIN something only people living in America need, or could it be quietly blocking your property sale, pension payment or bank account here in the UK?

David is a British citizen who co-owns a U.S. LLC with friends, and his wife is American. He keeps hearing “just get an ITIN” but nobody tells him which of his situations actually requires one.

The reasons the IRS recognises

On Form W-7 you must tick the reason that best fits your case. In practice the common reasons are:

  • A non-resident alien who needs an ITIN to claim a tax treaty benefit (box a).
  • A non-resident alien filing a U.S. federal tax return, including only to claim a refund (box b).
  • A U.S. resident alien under the substantial presence test who files a return but cannot get an SSN (box c).
  • A dependent of a U.S. citizen or resident alien (box d) – only where claimed for an allowable tax benefit.
  • The spouse of a U.S. citizen or resident alien, for example on a joint return (box e).
  • A non-resident alien student, professor or researcher (box f).
  • A dependent or spouse of a non-resident alien holding a U.S. visa (box g).
  • “Other” (box h): the five exceptions, for example partnership or LLC interests, a U.S. bank account, pension, 401(k) or annuity payments, royalties, mortgage interest, or the sale of U.S. property.
  • Renewal of an ITIN that has expired.

Return required – or an exception

Every ITIN needs a federal tax purpose. Most applicants attach a valid U.S. return to Form W-7. Five exceptions let you apply without a return, if you can prove the exception with supporting documents (for example a letter from your bank or withholding agent).

The wrong box delays everything

Choosing the wrong reason box or sending the wrong supporting document is one of the most common causes of delay. That is exactly where an acceptance agent saves time.

Practical takeaway

  • Match your situation to one reason box on Form W-7.
  • No return? You need a documented exception.
  • Not sure which box? Ask before you post anything.

A reader asks

“My U.S. broker says I need an ITIN for dividends, but my accountant says I don’t. Who’s right?”

It depends on whether the dividends are subject to IRS reporting or withholding this tax year and whether a withholding agent will certify that. We check this with you before you pay anything for the application.

title: ITIN vs SSN: Which Number Do You Actually Need?
description: ITIN vs SSN explained: who is eligible for a Social Security Number, when an SSA denial letter is needed, and when you can apply for an ITIN instead.
body:
Should you apply for a Social Security Number or an ITIN, and what happens if you pick the wrong one?

Amira is moving to the U.S. on a work visa next year but will first receive U.S. consulting income from the UK. Her adviser says “ITIN”, her future employer says “SSN”.

The simple rule

If you are eligible to obtain an SSN (for example a U.S. citizen or someone lawfully admitted for employment), you must not apply for an ITIN. An ITIN is only for people who must furnish a taxpayer ID but are not eligible for an SSN.

Visa or work permission? SSN first

If you enter the U.S. with a green card or visa that lets you work, apply for an SSN with the Social Security Administration (SSA) using Form SS-5. Anyone with an Employment Authorization Document (EAD), or already authorised to work, is eligible for an SSN. Only if the SSA rules you ineligible do you complete Form W-7, and the SSA’s letter of denial must be attached or your application will be rejected.

Don’t file while an SSN application is pending

If your SSN application is pending, do not file Form W-7. Wait for the SSA’s decision.

Students and honoraria visitors

F, J and M visa students who will not work, and visitors receiving only honoraria, do not need to go to the SSA first. A letter from the Designated School Official, Responsible Officer or Authorised School Official can be used instead.

Practical takeaway

  • Eligible for an SSN = no ITIN.
  • Work visa or EAD: SSN first; denial letter goes with Form W-7.
  • Non-working students and honoraria visitors can use a school official’s letter.

A reader asks

“I was refused an SSN last year. Is that letter still good enough?”

Send it to us and we will check it against your visa and the application. The proof must clearly show the SSA denied your request.

title: How to Apply for an ITIN from the UK: Step-by-Step
description: How to apply for an ITIN from the UK: Form W-7, passport, U.S. tax return or exception, IRS address, timings and your three application routes.
body:
Can you really get a U.S. taxpayer number from your kitchen table in Leeds without flying anywhere?

Tom needs an ITIN to claim a refund of U.S. tax withheld on his pension. He is worried about posting his passport to Texas.

Step 1 – Decide your reason

Pick the single Form W-7 reason box that best explains your case (see our guide to why people need an ITIN). A tax purpose is required.

Step 2 – Return or exception

Attach a valid U.S. federal income tax return (Form 1040, 1040-NR or 1040-X) unless you qualify for an exception, in which case you attach proof of that exception instead.

Step 3 – Prove identity and foreign status

An original passport (or a copy certified by the issuing agency) is the only stand-alone document. Without a passport you need at least two other current documents, one with a recent photograph.

Step 4 – Choose how to submit

  • By post to IRS ITIN Operations, P.O. Box 149342, Austin, TX 78714-9342 (use the street address with Mail Stop 6090-AUSC for private couriers).
  • At an IRS Taxpayer Assistance Center in the U.S. by appointment – not practical from the UK.
  • Through an IRS-authorised Certifying Acceptance Agent (CAA), who can authenticate eligible original documents and return them after the in-person review.

Timing

If your application is complete expect an IRS letter in about seven weeks, up to eleven during peak tax time (15 January–30 April) or when applying from abroad. Applications mailed from abroad can take considerably longer.

Practical takeaway

  • One reason box, one return or exception, proper ID.
  • Never use the return’s own mailing address – send the whole package to ITIN Operations in Austin.
  • Using an eligible UK Certifying Acceptance Agent route can normally avoid sending an authenticated passport to the IRS.

A reader asks

“Do I have to include my passport itself or will a photocopy do?”

The IRS only accepts originals or copies certified by the issuing agency. A certifying acceptance agent can check your original and return it immediately.

Ask us / start your application →

title: Certifying Acceptance Agent (CAA): Why Use One for Your ITIN?
description: What a Certifying Acceptance Agent does for a UK ITIN application: compliant document review, Form W-7 (COA), secure remote routes and no eligible original passport mailed to the IRS.
body:
Would you post your only passport to an IRS mail-processing centre in Texas and hope it comes back before your next trip?

Sam is travelling to Spain soon and cannot risk sending his passport to the IRS. He needs to know what a UK CAA can verify and what a remote appointment still requires.

Acceptance agents versus Certifying Acceptance Agents

Acceptance Agents (AAs) are individuals or organisations operating under a written agreement with the IRS to assist ITIN applicants. Certifying Acceptance Agents (CAAs) assume additional responsibility for reviewing eligible original documents or copies certified by the issuing agency and completing Form W-7 (COA), Certificate of Accuracy.

What a CAA can authenticate

  • For primary and secondary applicants: approved identity and foreign-status documents, except foreign military identification cards.
  • For dependents: passports and civil birth certificates only.
  • The CAA submits Form W-7, Form W-7 (COA), the attached return or exception evidence, and the required document copies. Only the IRS decides whether to issue the ITIN.

In person or secure remote route

At an in-person appointment, the CAA can inspect the eligible original and return it at the meeting. A video interview is permitted for the interview only: the CAA must still have the original identification document or an issuing-agency certified copy in their possession during that interview. A remote applicant therefore sends the document securely to the CAA, who arranges secure return after inspection. The eligible original does not need to be mailed onward to the IRS.

Costs

The IRS does not charge an application fee for an ITIN. A CAA may charge for professional services, document handling, tax-return preparation and agreed travel or courier costs.

Practical takeaway

  • Using a CAA can keep an eligible original passport out of IRS mail.
  • A video call does not replace the CAA's possession of the original or issuing-agency certified copy.
  • For dependents, CAA authentication is limited to passports and birth certificates.

A reader asks

“Can I hold my passport up to the camera and keep it with me?”

No. For a video interview, the CAA must possess the original or issuing-agency certified copy. We can instead arrange an in-person appointment or an agreed secure delivery and return route.

title: ITIN for Form 1040-NR: When a Non-Resident Alien Must File a U.S. Return
description: ITIN for Form 1040-NR: when a non-resident alien needs an ITIN, how box b works, claiming a refund and the documents you need.
body:
You have never lived in America but U.S. tax was taken from your income. How do you get it back – and why does the IRS want a number you don’t have?

Mei lives in Cambridge and received U.S. royalties with 30% withheld. She is not eligible for an SSN and wants to file to claim a refund.

Box b: non-resident alien filing a U.S. return

A non-resident alien individual not eligible for an SSN who is required to file a U.S. return, or who files only to claim a refund, applies on Form W-7 with the return attached (Form 1040-NR). Under this reason you must give your complete foreign address on line 3.

Documents

  • Original passport (valid, not expired) or certified copy.
  • Your U.S. return attached to Form W-7.
  • A foreign tax ID (for example a UK UTR or National Insurance number) on line 6b if you have one.

A filing purpose is essential

The IRS issues ITINs for a genuine federal tax purpose: a legal filing requirement, a refund claim, or reporting income even if no tax is due. A return that contains all zero entries generally will not show a purpose.

Estimated tax while you wait

If you receive income with no tax withheld you may need to make estimated payments even before you have an ITIN. Write “ITIN TO BE REQUESTED” where the ITIN or SSN is asked for. Do not file Form W-7 with the payment voucher.

Practical takeaway

  • Box b = non-resident alien filing a return; return attached to Form W-7.
  • Always provide your complete foreign address under box b.
  • No purpose, no ITIN: nil returns do not usually qualify.

A reader asks

“I’m not sure if I’m a resident or non-resident for U.S. tax. Does it change the form?”

Yes: it changes the reason box (b or c) and the proof you give. The substantial presence test decides it. Tell us your day-counts and we’ll confirm the correct route.

title: ITIN for an LLC Owner: What Counts as an LLC Interest?
description: ITIN for LLC members who are not U.S. residents: when an LLC agreement supports Exception 1(a), what pages to submit and how classification matters.
body:
You own part of a U.S. LLC from the UK and the accountant says “you’ll need an ITIN.” But for which of your three tax situations?

Olu is a one-third member of a Delaware LLC that owns a Florida rental. The LLC will issue him a Schedule K-1 and the bank needs a TIN.

Classification decides the route

How an LLC is taxed matters. Where an LLC is taxed as a partnership, a member who must be reported on IRS forms (such as Schedule K-1 or Form 8805) can use Exception 1(a) – third-party withholding on passive income – without attaching a tax return. If your LLC is taxed differently (for example a single-member disregarded entity), the ITIN normally travels with a filed return, and your U.S. tax adviser should confirm the filing position.

What to attach under Exception 1(a)

  • A copy of the portion of the partnership or LLC agreement showing the entity’s name, its EIN, and the applicant’s name and signature.
  • It must show the entity conducts business in the United States.
  • Reporting or withholding must take place within the current tax year.

How Form W-7 is completed

Tick box h and write “Exception 1(a) – A Partnership Interest” on the line. If you also claim a treaty benefit, tick box a and give the treaty country and article.

Practical takeaway

  • LLC taxed as partnership: Exception 1(a) with an LLC agreement extract.
  • Other LLC types: expect a return to be attached.
  • Reporting must happen this tax year.

A reader asks

“Can you tell me how my LLC is classified?”

We can see what your documents show, but classification is a U.S. entity-tax decision. We’ll tell you which route fits what you send, and flag when your U.S. tax adviser should confirm.

title: ITIN for a Partnership Interest: Schedule K-1, 8805 and 1042-S Explained
description: Holding an interest in a U.S. or foreign partnership that invests in the U.S.? How Exception 1(a) works, what forms trigger the need and what to submit.
body:
Your partnership is about to send you a K-1 – but they can’t file it without your tax ID. Do you have to complete a full U.S. tax return just to get one?

Helen is a limited partner in a U.S. real-estate fund. The fund administrator told her: “No TIN, no distribution.”

Why partnerships ask

Information-reporting and withholding rules require partnerships and other third parties to request a TIN so they can file forms such as Form 8805 (Foreign Partner’s Information Statement of Section 1446 Withholding Tax), Form 1042-S and Schedule K-1.

Exception 1(a) in a sentence

Partners of a U.S. or foreign partnership that invests in the U.S. and who own assets that generate income subject to reporting or withholding can apply without attaching a return, provided the entity’s agreement is supplied.

Your checklist

  • Passport (original or certified).
  • Extract of the partnership or LLC agreement showing entity name, EIN, and your name and signature.
  • Form W-7 with box h ticked and “Exception 1(a) – A Partnership Interest”.
  • If treaty benefits are claimed: box a as well, and the treaty country and article number.

Timing

The withholding or reporting must take place in the current tax year, so apply early: the IRS aims to respond in about seven weeks (longer at peak times or from abroad).

Practical takeaway

  • K-1, 8805 and 1042-S reporting are what trigger the TIN request.
  • Exception 1(a): no return needed, agreement extract required.
  • Apply early – distributions can be held until the ITIN arrives.

A reader asks

“Which page of the partnership agreement do you need?”

The page showing the partnership name, its EIN and your name and signature, plus enough to show the partnership does business in the U.S. Send what you have and we’ll tell you what’s missing.

title: ITIN for a U.S. Bank Account: When Do Banks Require One?
description: Opening an interest-bearing U.S. bank account from the UK? Exception 1(b) and 1(c) explained, with the exact bank letter needed to get an ITIN.
body:
A U.S. bank says it can’t open your account without a U.S. tax ID. Do you need a tax return you haven’t filed yet?

Raj, a UK dentist, wants to hold dollars in a U.S. interest-bearing account for a property purchase. The bank asked for an ITIN.

Interest reported to the IRS

Where an account generates interest subject to IRS information reporting and/or withholding, the bank needs your TIN. That makes “third-party withholding on passive income” – Exception 1 – the usual route.

Exception 1(b): business account

For an interest-bearing account that generates income effectively connected with your U.S. trade or business. Attach an original signed letter from the bank on letterhead, showing your name and stating you have opened a business account subject to IRS reporting and/or withholding on interest during the current tax year.

Exception 1(c): resident alien individual account

For individuals who are resident aliens for tax purposes and have opened an interest-bearing individual account. The bank letter wording is the same, referring to an individual deposit account.

Practical tips

  • Ask the bank for the letter before you apply – a self-written statement is not enough.
  • Write “Exception 1(b)” or “1(c)” on the box h line of Form W-7.
  • Check the letter names you exactly as your passport does.

Practical takeaway

  • Interest subject to IRS reporting = Exception 1(b) or 1(c).
  • The bank’s signed letter on letterhead is the key document.
  • Mismatched names between letter and passport cause delays.

A reader asks

“My bank only gave me an email. Is that enough?”

Usually not. The IRS looks for an original signed letter or document on official letterhead. We can send you a sample letter to give your bank.

title: ITIN for the Spouse of a U.S. Citizen or Resident: Joint Returns Explained
description: ITIN for the non-U.S. spouse of a U.S. citizen: box e, joint return, what to attach and what changed after 2017 for spouses and dependants.
body:
You’re married to an American and you live in Britain. Can you file jointly with your spouse without a Social Security Number?

Claire and her husband (a U.S. citizen working in London) want to file a joint U.S. return. Claire has no SSN and no right to work in the U.S.

The rule since 2018

Because the deduction for personal exemptions was suspended from tax year 2018, a spouse or dependant is not eligible for an ITIN unless they are claimed for an allowable tax benefit or file their own return. A spouse filing a joint return is one of those benefits.

Applying under box e

Tick box e (spouse of U.S. citizen/resident alien) and enter the U.S. spouse’s full name and SSN or ITIN. The U.S. return must be attached to Form W-7, showing joint filing.

Documents

  • Claire’s original passport (stand-alone proof of identity and foreign status), or a certified copy.
  • The joint U.S. return, attached to Form W-7.
  • Where Claire could work in the U.S. (visa or EAD), an SSA denial letter first.

An older exception to ignore

Spouses claimed as an exemption can only be so for tax years 2017 and earlier. For 2018 onwards it is the joint return (or another allowable tax benefit) that counts.

Practical takeaway

  • Spouses qualify through an allowable tax benefit, such as a joint return.
  • Box e needs your spouse’s name and SSN/ITIN.
  • Attach the joint return to Form W-7.

A reader asks

“We already filed separately last year. Can we switch to joint with an ITIN now?”

Often yes by amending, but it depends on the year and facts. Tell us what was filed and we’ll tell you how the ITIN application should be set up.

title: How to Renew an ITIN: Form W-7, Documents and What Not to Forget
description: How to renew an expired ITIN: when renewal is needed, line 6e/6f, attaching your return, original documents and name changes.
body:
Your accountant says your ITIN has expired and your U.S. return will be held up. Do you start from scratch?

Nadia got her ITIN in 2012 and has not filed a U.S. return in years. Her U.S. income is now being reported again.

Renew only if you need it for a return

ITINs only need to be renewed if there is a federal tax filing purpose for the ITIN. If it will not appear on a U.S. return, you do not need to renew it now.

What to send

  • Form W-7, ticking “Renew an existing ITIN” and completing lines 6e and 6f (your previous ITIN and the name it was issued under).
  • A valid U.S. federal tax return, unless you qualify for an exception.
  • Your original identification documents or copies certified by the issuing agency (and the SSA denial letter if applicable).

Changed your name?

If your legal name has changed since the ITIN was assigned, send a letter explaining the change with proof: a marriage licence, divorce certificate or an official court document. The name on Form W-7 should match what you will use on your return.

Where it is processed

Renewal applications are processed at the IRS Austin office. Original documents are returned within about 60 days of receipt and processing. Using a certifying acceptance agent avoids that wait for most documents.

Practical takeaway

  • Renew only if the ITIN is needed for a return.
  • Include your old ITIN on line 6f.
  • A name change needs supporting documents.

A reader asks

“I’ve lost my ITIN letter. Can I still renew?”

Often yes. If you do not know your ITIN, tick “No/Don’t know” on line 6e. Tell us what you remember and we’ll guide you.

title: Has My ITIN Expired? The Three-Year Rule and the Pre-2013 Rule
description: Check if your ITIN expired: the three consecutive tax years rule, ITINs assigned before 2013 and what happens to a return filed with an expired ITIN.
body:
You haven’t used your ITIN for a few years. Is it still valid, or will it sink your next return?

Mark’s ITIN was issued in 2015. He filed in 2019 and then nothing until now.

The three-year rule

An ITIN that has not been included on a U.S. federal return at least once in the last three consecutive tax years expires on 31 December of the third consecutive tax year. It must be renewed before it can be used again on a U.S. federal return.

The pre-2013 rule

ITINs assigned before 2013 that were never renewed have expired. Expired ITINs must be renewed to avoid delays in processing your return.

How to tell

  • Look at the year on your ITIN assignment letter.
  • List the tax years your ITIN appeared on a filed U.S. return.
  • Three consecutive years without use means expired; pre-2013 and never renewed also means expired.

What to do

Renew with Form W-7 and your return (unless an exception applies). See our renewal guide.

Practical takeaway

  • Unused for three consecutive tax years = expired on 31 December of the third.
  • Pre-2013 and not renewed = expired.
  • Renew when you need to file again.

A reader asks

“It expired but my U.S. return is due next week. What now?”

Do not file with the expired number. Contact us today and we will prepare the renewal so the return and Form W-7 go together.

title: ITIN for 401(k), Pension and Annuity Payments Received in the UK
description: Receiving a U.S. 401(k), pension or annuity while living in the UK? How Exception 1(d) works, the withholding agent letter and treaty benefits.
body:
A U.S. pension provider is holding back 30% of your payment because it has no TIN for you. How do you stop that?

Janet worked in Chicago for ten years and now lives in Surrey. Her 401(k) administrator says it needs an ITIN to pay distributions.

Who can use Exception 1(d)

People receiving distributions such as pensions, annuities, rental income, royalties or dividends during the current year who must give an ITIN to the withholding agent (an investment company, insurance company, financial institution and so on) so it can meet tax withholding and reporting duties.

Entitled to payments after a family member’s death?

You become eligible to apply once you are entitled to a payment or distribution subject to information reporting and withholding. Your application must include an original document or signed letter from the withholding agent, on official letterhead, showing your name and confirming an ITIN is needed for distributions during the current tax year.

Completing Form W-7

  • Tick box h and enter “Exception 1d – Pension Distributions” or “Exception 1d – Annuity Distributions”.
  • If you claim treaty benefits (the UK has a treaty with the U.S.), also tick box a and give the treaty country and article number.
  • Submit with your passport and the withholding agent’s letter – no tax return required.

Practical takeaway

  • Exception 1(d) = no return, but an agent’s letter on letterhead.
  • Say “Pension” or “Annuity” on the box h line.
  • Treaty claim? Add box a plus country and article.

A reader asks

“My plan administrator will only send a statement, not a letter. Will the IRS accept it?”

Self-generated income statements are only accepted with a copy of the contract or a letter in a postmarked envelope from the withholding agent. We can send you a sample letter to request.

title: ITIN for Selling a U.S. Property: FIRPTA Withholding and Exception 4
description: Selling U.S. real estate as a UK resident? How an ITIN works with FIRPTA withholding, Forms 8288, 8288-A and 8288-B and what to attach to Form W-7.
body:
Your buyer’s lawyer says part of the sale price will be withheld for the IRS unless you produce an ITIN. Is that money gone?

George is selling a Texas condo he bought as an investment. Completion is in six weeks.

What the withholding is

When a U.S. real property interest is acquired from a foreign person, the buyer or transferee generally has a withholding obligation. This collects tax the seller may owe. In some cases the seller applies for a withholding certificate to reduce or eliminate withholding. An ITIN is needed for this transaction.

Exception 4 documents

  • A completed Form 8288, 8288-A or 8288-B.
  • A copy of the real estate sales contract or settlement statement.
  • As the seller, copies of the buyer’s Forms 8288 and 8288-A.
  • For a notice of non-recognition: documents showing the date, parties and type of transfer (for example a deed or like-kind exchange identification).

Form W-7

Tick box h and enter “Exception 4 – Disposition of Real Property” (FIRPTA). No tax return is required with the application.

Timing risk

Start early. The ITIN takes about seven weeks in a normal period, so apply as soon as the contract is signed.

Practical takeaway

  • Exception 4 = no return, contract plus Forms 8288 series.
  • Apply as soon as you exchange contracts.
  • Fees for property sales are priced per application.

A reader asks

“Completion is in four weeks. Can you still do it?”

We’ll prioritise it, but the IRS’s processing time is outside our control. Contact us right away and we’ll tell you honestly what is realistic.

title: ITIN for Royalties, Rental Income and Dividends: Claiming UK Treaty Benefits
description: Receive U.S. royalties, rent or dividends in the UK? Learn how an ITIN with treaty benefits (box a plus Exception 1(d)) can reduce withholding.
body:
U.S. tax is being deducted from your royalties at the full rate. Does the UK–U.S. tax treaty really let you pay less – and what has an ITIN to do with it?

An author in Norwich is paid U.S. royalties. The publisher says it can only apply a reduced treaty rate if it has a taxpayer number.

Why the ITIN is needed

A non-resident alien eligible for a reduced withholding rate under an income tax treaty needs a TIN to claim it (see Publication 515 on withholding, and Publication 901 on U.S. tax treaties).

How to fill the form

  • Tick box a (non-resident alien required to get an ITIN to claim tax treaty benefit) and box h.
  • Enter the exception on the h line, for example “Exception 1(d) – Royalty Income”.
  • Enter the treaty country and treaty article number under ‘Additional information’.
  • The treaty country must match the foreign address on line 3.

What to submit

An original letter or signed statement from the withholding agent on letterhead showing your name and confirming that an ITIN is needed to pay you this tax year. Self-generated statements are accepted only with the contract or a postmarked letter from the agent.

Practical takeaway

  • Treaty claim = box a + box h.
  • Treaty country and article number are mandatory.
  • The payer’s letter on letterhead is the key evidence.

A reader asks

“I don’t know which treaty article applies to me. Can you tell me?”

We will identify the article from the type of income you describe and show it on your form. We recommend a tax adviser confirm the treaty position for complex cases.

title: ITIN for a Dependent Living Abroad or in the U.S.: Who Qualifies?
description: ITIN for dependants: allowable tax benefits, head of household, child credits, proof of U.S. residency and when Canada or Mexico dependants are treated differently.
body:
You’re a U.S. taxpayer in the UK with a child, parent or relative who has no SSN. Can you still claim them – and how?

Marcus is American, lives in Kent, and supports his mother in Mexico. His accountant asked him to “get an ITIN for Mum”.

Dependants need an allowable tax benefit

From tax year 2018, a dependant can only get (or renew) an ITIN if they are claimed for an allowable tax benefit and are listed on your U.S. return with the right schedule, form or checked box. Merely listing them is not enough.

Residency proof

Dependants must prove U.S. residency unless they are dependants of U.S. military personnel stationed overseas, or they are proving foreign status from Canada or Mexico and are claimed for a benefit other than the credit for other dependents (for example head of household). Others can show a passport with a U.S. date of entry, or one of: a U.S. school record, medical record, state ID, driving licence, visa, or (adults) a U.S. bank statement, rental statement or utility bill.

Documents

  • Passport (CAAs can verify passports and birth certificates for dependants).
  • Birth certificate for children under 18 unless a passport is used.
  • A photo ID for dependants aged 14 or over (18 for students).

Practical takeaway

  • No allowable tax benefit = no ITIN for a dependant.
  • Canada/Mexico dependants may be exempt from residency proof.
  • Check the ‘credit for other dependents’ box on the return yourself.

A reader asks

“My son is a U.S. citizen with a passport but no SSN. Does he need an ITIN?”

A U.S. citizen is eligible for an SSN and should not apply for an ITIN. Tell us about your son’s circumstances and we’ll point you to the right process.

title: What Is an “Allowable Tax Benefit” for ITIN Purposes? HOH, QSS, AOTC, PTC, CDCC and ODC
description: The seven allowable tax benefits that qualify a spouse or dependant for an ITIN, and the form or box that proves each one.
body:
You’ve listed your dependant on your return, but the IRS still rejected their ITIN. What did you miss?

Sofia’s tax software listed her niece as a dependant but didn’t tick the credit box because the niece had no ITIN yet.

The list

  • Joint return – spouse filing jointly.
  • Head of household (HOH) – tick the HOH filing status and list the applicant; they must have lived with you more than half the year or be your parent.
  • Qualifying surviving spouse (QSS) – your son, stepson, daughter or stepdaughter who lived with you all year.
  • American opportunity tax credit (AOTC) – attach Form 8863 listing the applicant.
  • Premium tax credit (PTC) – attach Form 8962.
  • Child and dependent care credit (CDCC) – attach Form 2441; allowed even if there is no tax to reduce.
  • Credit for other dependents (ODC) – the box next to the dependant’s name must be checked; dependant must be a U.S. resident or national.

The software trap

Listing a dependant is not an allowable benefit on its own. Tax software may not tick the ODC box for a dependant with no ID number. You must check it before sending the return with Form W-7.

HOH/QSS caution

An ITIN is not assigned or renewed for a HOH or QSS qualifying person who is not also claimed as a dependant on the attached return.

Practical takeaway

  • Seven benefits count; a dependant listing alone does not.
  • Check the ODC box yourself when using software.
  • Attach the form that matches the benefit (8863, 8962 or 2441).

A reader asks

“Can I claim the child tax credit with an ITIN?”

That is a separate U.S. tax question. For the ITIN, the benefits above are what the IRS looks for. We’ll tell you what to put on the application.

title: ITIN for Children: Birth Certificates, Medical Records and School Records
description: What documents are needed for a child’s ITIN: birth certificates, medical records under 6, school records up to 24 and photo ID rules.
body:
Your baby has a passport, a vaccination card and a red book from the health visitor. Which one does the IRS accept?

Elena is applying for her 4-year-old, who is British. She wonders whether UK health records count.

Under-18s: birth certificate unless passport

Dependants under 18 must prove foreign status and identity with a civil birth certificate, unless a passport is submitted. Under 14 (under 18 if a student), no photo ID is required.

Medical records – under 6 only

Official shot/immunisation record, or a signed, dated letter from the provider on letterhead. It must show name, date of birth, address, provider’s name and address, and care dated within 12 months of the W-7. Records are used for foreign status only if the documents are foreign. If proof of U.S. residency is needed, the address must be in the U.S.

School records – under 24

A report card, transcript, or signed, dated letter from a school official on letterhead showing name, address, school details and term dates ending no more than 12 months before the application.

Original needed

If you submit school or medical records, the original must go with the application whichever route you use. Electronic copies sent by the school can be printed clearly for submission.

Practical takeaway

  • Under 18: birth certificate or passport.
  • Medical records only for under-6s; school records only for under-24s.
  • Records must be within 12 months and complete.

A reader asks

“Our red book has handwritten entries. Is that OK?”

The record must show all required details and be clear. We’ll review it against the IRS checklist before submission.

title: ITIN for F-1, J-1 and M-1 Students: Scholarships, Fellowships and the SEVIS Letter
description: ITIN for international students: Exception 2(b) and 2(c) scholarships, the SEVIS certification letter, DSO letter and Form W-8BEN explained.
body:
You’ve won a scholarship at a U.S. university. The bursar needs a tax ID – but you can’t work and have no SSN. Now what?

Kai is a UK postgraduate visiting a U.S. university on a J-1 visa with a fellowship.

No SSN trip for non-working students

Students on F-1, J-1 or M-1 visas who will not work do not have to go to the SSA first. A letter from the Designated School Official or Responsible Officer stating you will not take employment or receive income from personal services can be used instead.

What the SEVIS certification letter must contain

  • Original letterhead with a verifiable address.
  • Applicant’s full name and SEVIS number, and confirmation of SEVIS registration.
  • That you presented an unexpired passport, visa or other ID (a U.S. visa is not needed if the foreign address is in Canada or Mexico), with the documents listed.
  • Signed and dated by a PDSO, DSO, RO or ARO, with a verifiable phone number.
  • Attached copies of the identity documents, and Form DS-2019 and/or I-20.

2(b) versus 2(c)

  • 2(b) – treaty benefit claimed: add Form W-8BEN, treaty country and article on Form W-7, and the award letter.
  • 2(c) – no treaty: add a DSO/RO letter that the income is non-compensatory and subject to IRS reporting this year.

Practical takeaway

  • Ask your DSO early – the SEVIS letter is the long pole.
  • 2(b) needs Form W-8BEN; 2(c) needs the DSO income letter.
  • A separate letter is needed for each applicant, including spouse and dependants.

A reader asks

“My university says it doesn’t know what a SEVIS certification letter is.”

We can send you a sample letter in the IRS format that your DSO can put on letterhead.

title: ITIN for Visiting Professors, Researchers and Honoraria Payments
description: Giving a lecture or research visit in the U.S.? How Exception 2(a) works for wages and honoraria, Form 8233 and the authorised school official letter.
body:
A U.S. university wants to pay you £2,000 for a three-day guest lecture. They can’t pay without your tax ID. Do you really need an SSN?

Prof. Ahmed is visiting New York for a conference on a B-1 visa and will be paid an honorarium.

Honoraria-only visitors

People present in the U.S. who receive only honoraria do not need to apply for an SSN or obtain an SSA denial letter. A letter from the Authorised School Official who extended the invitation, explaining the purpose of the visit and that an honorarium will be paid, is enough.

Wages or compensation under a treaty

For wages, salary, or compensation with treaty benefits you submit an employment letter, contract or invitation letter, the information on Form W-7 that you claim a treaty, and a completed Form 8233. Where you could work in the U.S. you also attach an SSA denial letter.

Filling in Form W-7

  • Box a (treaty) and box h with “Exception 2(a) – Honoraria Payment” or “Wages”.
  • Treaty country and article number.
  • Line 6g: the university or company, city and state, and your length of stay (it can be as short as a few days).

Practical takeaway

  • Honoraria-only visitors need the official’s letter, not an SSA letter.
  • Employment ITINs need Form 8233 and a contract or letter.
  • Don’t skip line 6g.

A reader asks

“I’m only visiting for two days. Do I really need to do all this?”

If the university must report or withhold on your payment this year, yes. We’ll review the letter you have and tell you what’s missing.

title: ITIN for a U.S. Mortgage: Exception 3 for First-Time Buyers
description: Buying a U.S. home from the UK? How Exception 3 lets you get an ITIN for mortgage-interest reporting without attaching a tax return.
body:
Your lender wants your ITIN to report your mortgage interest. You haven’t filed a U.S. return yet – can you still get one?

The Okafors are buying a holiday home in Orlando with a U.S. mortgage and are told: “Lender needs an ITIN before closing.”

Why the lender asks

Most home-mortgage lenders must report the interest they receive to both the IRS and the borrower on Form 1098 (Mortgage Interest Statement). First-time filers who secure a home loan can seek an ITIN to give to their lender.

What to provide

Documents showing evidence of a home mortgage loan on real property in the United States, such as a copy of the contract of sale or similar documentation. No tax return needs to be attached under this exception.

Form W-7

Tick box h and write “Exception 3 – Mortgage Interest”. Provide your passport and the mortgage evidence.

Practical takeaway

  • Exception 3 = no return, proof of a U.S. home mortgage.
  • Interest must be reported in the current tax year.
  • Apply as soon as the loan is secured.

A reader asks

“Can I wait to apply until after closing?”

Often the lender needs the number at or soon after closing. Contact us as soon as your loan is approved so timings line up.

title: Acceptable ITIN Documents: The 13 IRS-Approved IDs (and Why Passport Wins)
description: The 13 documents the IRS accepts for ITIN identity and foreign status, why a passport is the only stand-alone document, and when you need two.
body:
You have a UK driving licence, a utility bill and a bank statement. Surely that’s plenty for the IRS?

Daniel doesn’t want to part with his passport and thinks his UK driving licence and birth certificate will do.

The only list that matters

The IRS accepts 13 document types: passport (stand-alone); USCIS photo ID; U.S. Department of State visa; U.S. driving licence; U.S. military ID; foreign driving licence; foreign military ID; national ID card (current, with name, address, photo, date of birth and expiry); U.S. state ID; foreign voter’s registration card; civil birth certificate; medical records (dependants under 6); school records (dependants under 24).

Passport = stand-alone

A valid passport (or a certified copy) proves both identity and foreign status. For dependants, a passport without a U.S. date of entry cannot be the only document, except for dependants from Canada or Mexico or military dependants stationed overseas.

No passport? Two documents

Without a passport you must provide a combination of at least two current documents that show name and photograph and support your claim of foreign status. At least one must have a recent photograph, apart from children under 14 (under 18 if students).

Original or certified only

Originals, or copies certified by the issuing agency. Notarised copies are only accepted for dependants and spouses of U.S. military personnel applying from overseas. Copies of documents with information on both sides must show both sides.

Practical takeaway

  • Only 13 document types count.
  • Passport is the only stand-alone one.
  • Keep your originals safe – use a CAA.

A reader asks

“My UK driving licence and birth certificate: enough without a passport?”

Possibly, but a foreign driving licence mostly proves identity, while a civil birth certificate proves foreign status. We’ll check the combination against the table and tell you.

title: How Long Does an ITIN Take? Seven Weeks, Eleven Weeks or Longer from Abroad
description: ITIN processing times: seven weeks normally, up to eleven in peak season or from abroad, plus how to check status and what delays applications.
body:
You’ve sent your W-7 and it’s been six weeks. Is it lost, or is this normal?

Leila applied in February from London and is already nervous because her U.S. return is due in April.

The IRS timeframes

If the application is complete, the IRS aims to send an assignment letter in about seven weeks. During peak tax time (15 January–30 April), or when applying from abroad, it can take up to eleven weeks. Applications mailed from abroad may take considerably longer.

Getting your documents back

Originals are returned by the IRS (within about 60 days if you posted them). A prepaid express or courier envelope can speed return. If you used a CAA, your originals are back with you the same day.

What causes delay

  • Wrong reason box, or missing exception proof.
  • Name or date-of-birth mismatch between Form W-7 and your documents.
  • Expired documents, or missing visa pages.
  • Using the return’s own mailing address instead of ITIN Operations.

Checking status

If you haven’t heard after the referenced time, call the IRS (+1 267-941-1000 from outside the U.S., not toll-free). Keep a copy of everything you sent.

Practical takeaway

  • Plan for 7–11 weeks, longer from abroad.
  • Mistakes cause most delays, not the IRS queue.
  • Apply well before any deadline.

A reader asks

“Can you speed it up?”

We can’t change how fast the IRS works, but a correct, complete application, and no loss of time getting your originals back, is the best way to avoid avoidable delay.

title: Can You E-File With a New ITIN? The “Year Received” Rule
description: E-filing with an ITIN: why you cannot e-file in the year you receive it, how many prior years you can e-file, and what to do instead.
body:
You’ve just got your ITIN letter. You open your tax software… and it won’t let you file. Why?

Ben got his ITIN in March and tried to e-file immediately.

The rule

You can only e-file a return using an ITIN in the calendar year after the year in which you received it. If you apply and receive an ITIN this year, you may not e-file any return (including prior-year returns) with that ITIN until next year.

Prior-year limits

Because of IRS e-file limits, you can only e-file the current tax year and two prior tax years.

So what do you do?

Your first return with the new ITIN is usually the paper return you attach to Form W-7. For later returns, check the year rule before choosing e-file.

Extensions and payments

Do not file Form W-7 with extension requests (Form 4868 or 2688) or estimated payments (1040-ES). Write “ITIN TO BE REQUESTED” where the ITIN or SSN is requested instead.

Practical takeaway

  • No e-file in the calendar year you receive the ITIN.
  • E-file works for the current and two prior years.
  • Never send W-7 with extension or estimate forms.

A reader asks

“I need to file an amended return. Can I e-file it?”

That depends on the tax year and the type of return. Tell us what you are filing and when you received your ITIN, and we’ll confirm whether e-filing is allowed.

title: Form W-7 Line by Line: The Most Common Mistakes (and How to Avoid Them)
description: Form W-7 explained line by line: name, addresses, date of entry, visa, previous ITIN and signature rules, with the mistakes that cause rejections.
body:
You’ve spent an evening filling in Form W-7 and the IRS sends it back. Which line tripped you up?

Ruth’s application was rejected because her foreign address was a PO box.

The traps

  • Line 1a: name exactly as on your documents; it must match your tax return. 1b is your birth name if different.
  • Line 2: a complete mailing address – the IRS uses it to return documents and send letters.
  • Line 3: your permanent foreign address. No PO boxes or ‘c/o’ addresses. If you no longer have a permanent foreign residence, enter just the country (but under reason b give the full foreign address).
  • Line 4: date of birth as MM/DD/YYYY, plus country of birth.
  • Line 6c/6d: visa class, number, expiry; document type, issuer, number, expiry and U.S. entry date. If you have never entered, write “Never entered the United States”.
  • Line 6e/6f: a previous ITIN or IRSN – required for renewals.
  • Line 6g: only if box f – college or company, city, and length of stay.

Check every line

If any field is blank or invalid, the application will be suspended or rejected. Enter N/A where something does not apply.

Made a mistake after submitting?

Do not file another Form W-7. Wait for the IRS to write to you and send the correct information with your reply.

Who signs

The applicant signs. For under-18s a parent or court-appointed guardian signs; a power of attorney must be on IRS Form 2848. If someone cannot sign their name they sign a mark in front of a witness, who also signs.

Practical takeaway

  • No PO boxes or ‘c/o’ on line 3.
  • Dates are MM/DD/YYYY; entry date must be complete.
  • Don’t re-submit a corrected form – reply to the IRS letter.

A reader asks

“Can I use the old version of Form W-7 I have saved?”

No. Use the current version; older versions can delay processing or be returned. We use the latest one.

title: ITIN for a Deceased Taxpayer: What the Executor or Spouse Must Send
description: Applying for an ITIN for someone who has died: ‘Deceased’ on Form W-7, who can apply, and the documents needed for surviving spouses, executors and others.
body:
A relative abroad has died and left a U.S. tax refund unclaimed. Can you still get them an ITIN?

Fatima is the executor of her father’s UK estate; he had U.S. dividend income.

How to mark Form W-7

Write the word “Deceased” and the date of death across the top of Form W-7.

Three situations

  • Surviving spouse filing an original or amended joint return: Form W-7, return, and documents proving identity and foreign status of the deceased.
  • Court-appointed executor/administrator filing an original return: the same, plus a court certificate showing your appointment.
  • Someone else claiming a refund on a joint return where no executor was appointed: the same documents plus Form 1310 and a copy of the death certificate.

Children who died

If Form W-7 is for a deceased taxpayer under 18, one document must be a birth certificate unless a passport with a U.S. entry date is provided.

Practical takeaway

  • Write ‘Deceased’ and the date of death on Form W-7.
  • Documents depend on who you are.
  • Form 1310 and a death certificate apply where no executor is appointed.

“Which case am I?”

Tell us your relationship to the person and whether an executor was appointed. We’ll confirm which documents the IRS needs.

title: Does an ITIN Let You Work in the U.S.? No – and Here’s What to Do If You Can Work
description: An ITIN does not authorise U.S. employment or change immigration status. Learn when to get an SSN instead and how EADs and student visas affect you.
body:
A friend says “just get an ITIN and you can work.” Is that true? Spoiler: no.

Yusuf arrives on an F-1 visa and wants to take a campus job. A classmate told him to apply for an ITIN.

What an ITIN can’t do

An ITIN does not authorise work in the U.S. It is not valid for employment purposes, it does not change your immigration status and it does not entitle you to Social Security benefits or the Earned Income Tax Credit.

If you are allowed to work

Certain non-immigrant statuses authorise work, and some people must apply to USCIS for an Employment Authorization Document (EAD). Anyone with an EAD, or already authorised to work, is eligible for an SSN and should not apply for an ITIN unless the SSA rejects the SSN request, in which case the denial letter must be attached.

Students

Whether a student may work is set by USCIS rules; check with your Designated School Official or uscis.gov. Students who are eligible to work and will be employed should apply for an SSN; if denied, they may apply for an ITIN with the denial attached.

Practical takeaway

  • ITIN ≠ work permission.
  • Authorised to work? SSN first.
  • Use your DSO or USCIS for work-permission questions.

title: ITIN Help in Bedford, Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Buckinghamshire and London
description: Home and office visits for ITIN ID verification across Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Buckinghamshire, plus Luton, Heathrow, London and St Pancras. Fixed fees, no VAT.
body:
Need your passport checked for an ITIN but can’t take time off work? Can an acceptance agent really come to your home or office – even at lunchtime?

Ana works in Bedford and can only spare her lunch hour. She wants her passport verified without taking a day off.

Where we meet

  • Home visits and office visits: we are flexible. If you are at work we can arrange the ID verification around your lunch break, or any time that suits you.
  • Bedford area: no travel charges, whether at your home, office or a public venue.
  • Milton Keynes: £20 travel charge.
  • Luton Airport meeting spot: £25 additional travel.
  • London location: £40 travel.
  • St Pancras station and central London: £45 additional travel.
  • Heathrow Airport meeting spot: £55 additional travel.
  • Europe: additional travel costs quoted by location.

Bedfordshire, Hertfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Buckinghamshire

We cover all four counties. Outside the Bedford area, a travel charge applies to cover the representative’s travel time and costs to visit you and collect your documents. For surrounding areas we confirm the travel cost by email before you pay.

Not near any of these?

We cover the whole UK. Choose “Elsewhere” on the form and one of our team will confirm availability and any travel charge.

Prefer to post your passport?

You can send your original passport to us and we return it by secure post. DHL charges a standard £60, and DHL/FedEx charges apply for other services.

Fixed ITIN service fees

  • Spouse of a US citizen: £395.
  • ITIN renewal: £395.
  • ITIN with an already prepared 1040-NR tax return: £395.
  • LLC: £425.
  • LLC owners with a US bank account: £425; an LLC and EIN are required.
  • Partnership: £450.
  • Sale of US property / FIRPTA: £450.
  • 401(k), US estate income or pension plan: £495.
  • Wages, scholarship or complex treaty-based compensation: £550.
  • Other ITIN categories: £425.

All fees are all-inclusive, with no VAT, for the Form W-7 / CAA service only. US tax return preparation is separately quoted. EIN applications are a separate service at £375 all-inclusive, no VAT. For additional travel or courier charges, email Taz@itinpro.uk or Shan@itinpro.uk for a customised, itemised invoice. If your ITIN category is not listed, select Other and pay £425. Explain your circumstances in the application notes or by email; any fee difference will be confirmed and invoiced separately for payment later.

Practical takeaway

  • Six UK meeting points, plus Europe and ‘other UK’.
  • Posting your passport is possible, with secure return.
  • Fees start at £395, all-inclusive, no VAT.

A reader asks

“I live in Edinburgh. Can you help?”

Yes: choose ‘Elsewhere’ or the postal option in the form. One of the team will get back to you with the best way to verify your documents and any travel cost.
